questions.question: Which organization led the development and manufacturing of Korea's domestically developed Earth observation satellite, CAS500-2?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Korea Aerospace Industries**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Korea's** domestically developed Earth observation satellite, the **Compact Advanced Satellite 500-2 (CAS500-2)**, was successfully launched into space aboard a **SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI)** led the development and manufacturing of **CAS500-2**. This marks the first time a Korean mid-sized Earth observation satellite of this class was developed independently by a private entity.
 
• The **Korea Aerospace Research Institute** is incorrect because while it was a joint design partner on the previous **CAS500-1** project, KAI absorbed the core technologies to develop the second unit independently.
 
• The **Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA)** is the national space agency overseeing the mission's progress, not the manufacturer.
 
• **SpaceX** provided the **Falcon 9 launch vehicle**, but was not involved in the satellite's manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The satellite was launched from the **Vandenberg Space Force Base** in **California, United States**.
 
• It successfully entered a **sun-synchronous orbit** at an altitude of **498 kilometers (309 miles)**.
 
• The mission faced a nearly four-year delay due to the **Russia-Ukraine war**, as it was originally scheduled to launch in 2022 aboard a **Russian Soyuz rocket**.
 
• The satellite established its first communication link with a ground station in **Svalbard, Norway**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **CAS500-2** is tasked with **national land management** and **disaster monitoring**, including tracking environmental changes and providing rapid imagery response to natural disasters.
 
• Eighty-six percent of the satellite platform and 98 percent of the payload technology were developed domestically in Korea.
 
• The Korean government plans to use CAS500-2 to enter the international satellite export market, targeting countries like **Saudi Arabia, Peru, and Indonesia**.

questions.question: The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) connects India with which regions, providing a multimodal transport link for trade and economic cooperation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Asia and Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) is a multimodal transportation network that connects India with **Central Asia, Russia, and Europe**.
 
• The corridor spans approximately **7,200 kilometers** and uses a combination of rail, road, and sea routes to facilitate trade.
 
• INSTC was established under an agreement signed in **2000 by India, Iran, and Russia**, with several additional member states joining later.
 
• The primary objective of the INSTC is to reduce the time and cost of transporting goods between India and regions like **Russia, Central Asia, and Europe**.
 
• This corridor plays a crucial role in enhancing **economic cooperation**, trade connectivity, and geopolitical ties between the member countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **South-East Asia**
 
 
• South-East Asia refers to the region comprising countries like Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, and the Philippines.
 
• This region is not directly connected to the INSTC; however, India engages in trade and connectivity through initiatives like the **India-ASEAN Free Trade Agreement** and the **Act East Policy**.
 
• India is also part of the **Mekong-Ganga Cooperation**, aimed at enhancing trade and cultural ties with South-East Asia.
 
 
 
• **Africa**
 
 
• Africa is a key partner for India in areas like trade, investment, and development cooperation.
 
• India has launched initiatives such as the **Asia-Africa Growth Corridor (AAGC)** to enhance connectivity and economic integration with African nations.
 
• However, Africa is not part of the INSTC network.
 
 
 
• **Australia**
 
 
• Australia is a major partner for India in trade and strategic cooperation, especially under the **India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA)**.
 
• India and Australia collaborate in sectors like education, energy, and defense under the **Quad framework** (along with the US and Japan).
 
• Despite its importance to India, Australia is geographically disconnected from the INSTC framework.
 
 
 
• **INSTC Overview**
 
 
• The INSTC provides an alternative to traditional shipping routes through the Suez Canal by significantly reducing **transportation time and costs**.
 
• India uses ports like **Mumbai and Mundra** to connect with Iran's Bandar Abbas port, which serves as a gateway to Central Asia and Russia via rail and road networks.
 
• The corridor enhances India's access to **strategic markets** and contributes to its broader geopolitical and economic ambitions.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The United States has completed its withdrawal from the World Health Organization, ending its membership for the first time since which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1948.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The United States has ended its membership in the World Health Organization for the first time since the organization was established in 1948.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The World Health Organization was founded in 1948, with the United States as a founding member.**
 
• The U.S. announced its plan to leave the WHO on January 20, 2025.
 
• The withdrawal process lasted one year and involved halting funding and withdrawing personnel.
 
• The decision was taken citing WHO’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic and lack of institutional reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• World Health Organization__

 __
 
• A specialized agency of the United Nations established in 1948.
 
• Coordinates international efforts on disease control and public health emergencies.
 
 
 
• United States and WHO__
 __
 
• The U.S. was historically one of the largest contributors to the WHO.
 
• The withdrawal marks a significant shift in global health cooperation.
 
 
 
• Global Health Governance__
 
 
• Refers to international coordination to address global health challenges.
 
• Has faced scrutiny following the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question: Which of the following global cities was officially declared the World Book Capital 2025 by UNESCO in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rio de Janeiro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rio de Janeiro (Brazil)** was officially designated as the **UNESCO World Book Capital 2025**.
 
• The title became effective on **23 April 2025**, which is observed annually as **World Book and Copyright Day**.
 
• UNESCO selected Rio de Janeiro in recognition of its comprehensive programme to promote **reading, literacy, publishing, and equitable access to books** across all sections of society.
 
• The city's initiatives focus on encouraging a culture of reading, strengthening libraries, and making books accessible, especially to young people and underserved communities.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3 – Rio de Janeiro**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO World Book Capital:**

 
 
• It is an annual designation awarded by **UNESCO** to a city that demonstrates excellence in promoting books and reading.
 
• The selected city holds the title for one year, beginning on **23 April**.
 
 
 
• **Previous World Book Capitals:**
 
 
• **2024:** Strasbourg, France.
 
• **2025:** Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
 
 
 
• **World Book and Copyright Day:**
 
 
• Celebrated every year on **23 April** to promote reading, publishing, and the protection of intellectual property through copyright.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Book Capital 2025:** **Rio de Janeiro, Brazil**.
 
• **Title Effective From:** **23 April 2025**.
 
• **Declared By:** **UNESCO**.
 
• **Purpose:** To promote reading, books, publishing, and literacy worldwide.
 
• **Previous World Book Capital (2024):** **Strasbourg, France**.

questions.question: Which country has imposed a 13% value-added tax on condoms and contraceptive drugs from January 1, 2026, as part of efforts to boost its declining birth rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **China removed a three-decade-old tax exemption on condoms and contraceptive drugs to encourage higher birth rates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **China imposed a 13% value-added tax on condoms and contraceptive pills from January 1, 2026.**
 
• The tax exemption had been in place for nearly 30 years.
 
• The move aims to address China’s declining birth rate.
 
• China’s population fell for the third consecutive year in 2024.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Demographic Context__

 __
 
• China has experienced falling birth rates for decades.
 
• Decline attributed to the former one-child policy, urbanisation and rising living costs.
 
• High childcare and education expenses discourage family formation.
 
 
 
• Government Measures__
 __
 
• Childcare subsidies exempted from personal income tax.
 
• Annual childcare subsidy introduced in 2024.
 
• Promotion of positive marriage and childbearing attitudes through policy messaging.
 
 
 
• Policy Significance__
 
 
• Reflects China’s shift towards fertility-friendly economic policies.
 
• Part of broader efforts announced at the Central Economic Work Conference.
 
• Aims to stabilise population decline in the long term.

questions.question: What is the annual supply volume of liquefied natural gas (LNG) agreed upon in the 20-year deal signed between Malaysia’s Petronas and Japan’s JERA?

questions.question: Which of the following nations has been elected to serve as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the first time since joining the United Nations in 1992?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kyrgyzstan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**
__
• The **United Nations General Assembly** elected five countries to join the **15-member Security Council** as non-permanent members for a two-year term starting in **2027**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**
__
• **Kyrgyzstan**: The election marks a historic milestone for Kyrgyzstan, as it will serve on the **Security Council** for the **first time** since it joined the **United Nations in 1992**.
• **Other Elected Members**: Alongside Kyrgyzstan, **Zimbabwe** (elected unopposed for the African Group), **Austria**, **Portugal**, and **Trinidad and Tobago** were also elected.
• **Term Duration**: These five nations will serve a **two-year term** starting on **1 January 2027**.
• **Germany**: Germany lobbied for a seat but failed, coming **third** for the two places contested by the **Western European and Others Group**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
__
• **Permanent Members**: The Security Council has five permanent members with **veto power**: **Britain, China, France, Russia, and the United States**.
• **Outgoing Members**: Countries leaving at the end of 2026 include **Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama**, and **Somalia** (whom Zimbabwe will replace).
• **Continuing Members**: **Bahrain, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia, and Liberia** will remain on the council until the end of **2027**.
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• The **Security Council** is the only **UN body** capable of making **legally binding decisions**, such as imposing **sanctions** or authorizing the **use of force**.
• The newly elected members represent various regional groups: **African Group**, **Western European and Others Group**, and others.</ul

questions.question: Which country has launched a 500MW floating solar project at the Kariba Dam to address power shortages and receding water levels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zimbabwe.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Zimbabwe has officially launched a 500MW floating solar project at the Kariba Dam to combat chronic power shortages caused by climate change.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capacity:** The project aims for a total of **500MW**, starting with a **250MW pilot phase**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** It utilizes the Kariba Dam's underutilized **1,200MW transmission capacity**, which has struggled to carry more than 400MW due to low water levels.
 
• **Hybrid Model:** The system combines daytime solar power with nighttime hydropower to ensure a stable energy supply.
 
• **Climate Resilience:** Floating panels (floatovoltaics) help **reduce water evaporation** from Lake Kariba and benefit from water-cooling for higher efficiency.
 
• **Economic Integration:** The project includes **aquaculture (fish farming)** beneath the panels and generates **carbon credits** for industrial users.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Financing:**__ **Afreximbank** (African Export-Import Bank) is providing a **$4.4 million** facility for feasibility studies.
 
• __**PPA:**__ A 20-year Power Purchase Agreement has been signed by the **Intensive Energy Users Group** (large miners and industries).
 
• __**Location:**__ Lake Kariba is the world's largest man-made lake by volume, located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

questions.question: What major change in its postwar pacifist policy did Japan's Cabinet approve in April 2026?

options.text: Ending the deployment of overseas peacekeeping troops
Scrapping the ban on lethal weapons exports
Banning the import of foreign defense equipment
Reducing the domestic production of fighter jets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scrapping the ban on lethal weapons exports**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• On **April 21, 2026**, **Japan** officially endorsed **scrapping a ban on lethal weapons exports**.
 
• This move represents a major change to the country's longstanding **postwar pacifist policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Policy Shift:** The approval of the new guideline clears a final set of hurdles for **Japan's postwar arms sales**. By scrapping these limits, **Japan** will now allow the export of lethal equipment.
 
• **Allowed Equipment:** Under the revised framework, the export of specific military hardware such as **fighter jets**, **missiles**, and **destroyers** is now permitted.
 
• **Options Analysis:** **Scrapping the ban on lethal weapons exports** is the correct answer because it directly addresses the cabinet's endorsed action to overhaul its pacifist constraints. The other options regarding troop deployments, banning imports, or reducing production are not supported by the recent guideline changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Leadership:** The new guideline was approved by the Cabinet led by **Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi**.
 
• **Strategic Goals:** The primary objective behind this historic shift is to build up **Japan's arms industry** and to significantly deepen cooperation with its **defense partners**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The endorsement by **Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's Cabinet** marks a definitive departure from decades of self-imposed restrictions on **lethal weapons exports**.
 
• This decision will facilitate the global sale of advanced Japanese defense equipment, including **fighter jets** and **missiles**, to strengthen strategic alliances.

questions.question: The term “Partnership for Indo-Pacific Industrial Resilience (PIPIR)”, recently seen in the news, refers to:

options.text: A plurilateral defence arrangement under NATO aimed at expanding collective security operations into the Indo-Pacific region.
A multilateral initiative under the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework for Prosperity (IPEF) to strengthen resilient and diversified supply chains.
A regional trade bloc established under ASEAN to harmonise tariff structures and promote free trade among Indo-Pacific nations.
A financial facility created by the IMF to support industrial reconstruction and crisis recovery in Indo-Pacific economies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The U.S. led PIPIR is exploring funding for defence manufacturing infrastructure in the Philippines, highlighting its growing strategic-economic significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• PIPIR is a multilateral initiative launched in May 2024 under the IPEF framework to enhance industrial resilience and secure supply chains. **Hence, Option B is correct. **
 
• It is not a defence alliance under NATO; rather, it focuses on economic and industrial cooperation. **Hence, Option A is incorrect. **
 
• It is not an ASEAN-based trade bloc and does not deal with tariff harmonisation or free trade agreements. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **
 
• It is not an IMF-led financial facility, but a collaborative initiative focused on supply chains and industrial resilience. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The initiative complements broader efforts under IPEF to strengthen economic cooperation without being a traditional trade agreement.
 
• India is not a formal member but remains relevant for potential collaboration in supply chain diversification.
 
• It seeks to build a trusted network for information sharing and technical cooperation among partner countries.
 
• Taiwan participates in an advisory capacity, indicating flexibility in engagement beyond formal membership structures.

questions.question: Which country has approved the world's first commercial stem-cell therapies for Parkinson's and heart failure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Japan has officially approved the first commercial medical products derived from induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) cells for treating Parkinson’s and heart failure.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Parkinson’s treatment, named Amchepry, replaces lost dopamine-producing cells in the brain using stem-cell precursors.**
 
• **The heart failure treatment, ReHeart, consists of heart muscle sheets designed to form new blood vessels and restore function.**
 
• **These breakthroughs are based on the Nobel Prize-winning research of Shinya Yamanaka (2012), who discovered how to revert mature cells to a pluripotent state.**
 
• **Both therapies have received provisional licenses and are expected to be clinically available by Summer 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• iPS Cells__

 __
 
• Induced Pluripotent Stem cells are adult cells that have been genetically reprogrammed to an embryonic stem cell-like state.
 
 
 
• Shinya Yamanaka__
 __
 
• A Japanese scientist who won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery that mature cells can be reprogrammed to become pluripotent.
 
 
 
• Dopamine__
 __
 
• A neurotransmitter in the brain; the loss of dopamine-producing cells is the primary cause of Parkinson's disease symptoms.
 
 
 
• Provisional License__
 
 
• A conditional approval that allows earlier access to innovative treatments while long-term data continues to be collected.

questions.question: The term “Axis of Evil”, recently seen in the context of West Asian geopolitics, refers to:

options.text: A military alliance formed by Iran, Syria, and Hezbollah.
A regional bloc comprising Iran, Iraq, and Syria opposing Israel.
A term used by the United States to describe Iran, Iraq, and North Korea.
A strategic grouping of Russia, China, and Iran against NATO.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The ongoing Iran–Israel tensions have revived references to historical U.S. foreign policy doctrines, including the term “Axis of Evil.”

questions.question: Finland became the _____ European country to exit the Ottawa landmine treaty in June 2025.
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**5th**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • **Finland** became the **5th European country** to exit the **Ottawa Landmine Treaty** in **June 2025**. • The **Ottawa Treaty**, also known as the **Mine Ban Treaty**, was adopted in **1997** to prohibit the use, stockpiling, production, and transfer of anti-personnel landmines. • Countries exiting the treaty typically cite concerns about **national security** and the need for landmines in specific **defense strategies** as reasons for withdrawal. • Prior to Finland, four other European nations had already exited the treaty, demonstrating a growing trend of nations reconsidering their commitments due to evolving **geopolitical threats**. • Finland's decision was influenced by its unique **geographic location** and **security considerations**, especially in light of tensions in the **Nordic-Baltic region**.

questions.question: The International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), primarily empowers the U.S. President to:

options.text: Regulate and block transactions during a declared national emergency involving foreign threats, but not to impose tariffs.
Unilaterally impose import tariffs of any magnitude and duration without congressional authorisation.
Levy customs duties and trade taxes as part of routine trade policy under executive discretion.
Replace congressional trade legislation in matters of national security and commerce.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the President’s use of the IEEPA to impose tariffs was not in accordance with law, holding that the statute does not authorise the imposition of tariffs, thereby reaffirming checks and balances on executive power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• IEEPA authorises the U.S. President to regulate, block, or prohibit certain transactions and property interests during declared national emergencies involving foreign threats. **Hence, Option A is correct. **
 
• IEEPA does not authorise the imposition of tariffs or customs duties; such powers must be clearly conferred by Congress under trade statutes. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• Routine trade taxation and customs duties fall under specific trade laws and congressional authority, not IEEPA. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **
 
• IEEPA cannot substitute for congressional trade legislation; executive powers remain bounded by statutory limits. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, 1962 allows tariffs on national security grounds.
 
• Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 permits temporary tariffs in specific balance-of-payments emergencies.
 
• Checks and balances in the U.S. system limit unilateral executive trade actions without clear statutory basis.
 
• WTO disciplines require members to justify trade measures under permitted exceptions.

questions.question: Which insects have become the first in the world to be granted legal rights, including the right to exist, flourish & be legally protected?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amazonian stingless bees.**__

__
 
• **Amazonian stingless bees have been legally recognised with inherent rights for the first time globally.**
 
• The recognition was adopted through a municipal ordinance by the provincial municipality of Satipo in Peru.
 
• The Declaration grants them rights such as the right to exist, flourish, regenerate natural cycles, and live in a pollution-free habitat.
 
• Amazonian Stingless Bees__ 
 __
 
• Do not possess stingers, unlike European bees
 
• Oldest bee species on Earth
 
• Pollinate over 80 per cent of Amazonian flora
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__

 __
 
• Recognises legal rights of stingless bees and their ecosystems
 
• Includes rights to healthy populations, habitat restoration and legal representation
 
• Establishes a precedent under the global Rights of Nature movement
 
 
 
• Ecological Importance__
 __
 
• Key pollinators sustaining rainforest biodiversity
 
• Support crops like coffee, chocolate, avocados and blueberries
 
• Vital to ecological, social and cultural practices of Indigenous Amazonian communities
 
 
 
• Threats Faced__
 
 
• Climate change and deforestation
 
• Pesticide use
 
• Competition from European bee species
